content: To edit a page on Wikipedia, you simply need to click the edit this page tab located at the top of the page or use a section-edit link. This action will open a new page containing a text box with the editable content of the original page. Below the text box, there is a small field where you should write a concise edit summary to describe the changes you are making. You can use shorthand notations for this purpose, as explained in the legend. Before saving your changes, you can preview the differences between your edits and the previous version of the page by clicking the Show changes button. If you are satisfied with the modifications, you can confidently press the Save page button, making your changes immediately visible to all Wikipedia users. If you wish to view or participate in discussions about the page, you can click the Discussion tab to access the corresponding talk page. On this page, you can read comments from other Wikipedia users or add your own by clicking the + tab to create a new section. You can also edit the talk page in the same way as an article page. When contributing to talk pages or special-purpose project pages, it is important to sign your messages using four tildes (~~~~). However, you should not sign edits made to regular articles. The MediaWiki software automatically tracks which user makes each change in the page history. When making minor edits, such as correcting typos, adjusting formatting, or rearranging text without altering the content, you can check the minor edit box. This indicates that the changes are superficial and unlikely to be disputed. The minor edit option is only available to registered users. In contrast, major edits involve changes that affect the meaning of the article, even if the modification is as small as a single word. Before making major edits, it is advisable to discuss your proposed changes on the article's talk page. If you are working on a major edit over an extended period, you can use the {{inuse}} tag to minimize the risk of edit conflicts. Once the edit is complete, providing a detailed edit summary will help document the changes and facilitate review by other editors. Wikipedia uses a syntax system called wiki markup for formatting pages. For detailed guidance on wiki markup, you can refer to the Help:Editing page or the Help:Wikitext examples page. To include images in an article, you must upload them to Wikipedia using the upload page. Uploaded images can be found on the image list. It is important to adhere to Wikipedia's image use policy when adding images to articles. For more advanced image formatting options, you can consult the Extended image syntax guide. Headings in Wikipedia are created by placing text on a separate line and surrounding it with equal signs. For example, a top-level heading uses '==', while subheadings use '===', '====', and so on. For character formatting, Wikipedia provides various options, including the ability to display text exactly as typed (what-you-see-is-what-you-get formatting). Hidden comments can also be added within the text of an article using a specific format, although this practice is uncommon. When a page contains at least four headings, a table of contents (TOC) is automatically generated and placed before the first heading or after introductory sections. You can control the placement of the TOC by using the __TOC__ or __NOTOC__ commands. Wikipedia also supports the creation of tables using either special wiki markup or standard HTML elements. For guidance on when to use tables and how to create them, you can refer to the Help:Table page. Wikipedia includes a feature called templates, which allows standardized text or boilerplate content to be inserted into articles. For example, typing {{stub}} will display a message indicating that the article is a stub and inviting users to expand it. There are many templates available for specific purposes, such as {{disambig}} for disambiguation pages or {{sectstub}} for section stubs. A comprehensive list of templates can be found on the Wikipedia:Template messages page. For additional information on editing Wikipedia pages, you can explore resources such as the Wikipedia:Editing FAQ, the Wikipedia:Cheatsheet, and the Wikipedia:Manual of Style. These resources provide guidance on starting a new page, contributing effectively, and adhering to Wikipedia's style conventions. If you are creating an article about a specific topic, you may also want to check if there is a relevant WikiProject and follow its guidelines.
